acceptanceCriteria.text: A chat whose `<agent display name> · <title>` exceeds 120 characters starts: the grant label passed to issueChatCli/issueReachCli is at most 120 characters, starts with the agent display name, and does not end in a lone surrogate (regression test named in evidence fails before the fix and passes after).
The 120-character grant label limit is defined once and used by both the issueGrant schema and the chat grant label builder; the limit itself is unchanged.
Chats whose label already fits keep the exact `<agent display name> · <title>` label (covered by a test).
Full gate passes: npm run lint, npm test, npm run fireguard (not F), npm run typecheck, npm run deadcode, npm run build.

body:
## Bug

Starting an orchestrator chat for a queued run fails before the agent is spawned:

> Run #1 is queued, but skitarii could not be started: Invalid issueGrant input at label: Too big: expected string to have <=120 characters. It is waiting for an orchestrator.

## Cause (verified)

- `src/main/terminals/terminalSessions.ts` `runStart` builds the chat grant as `label: `${agent.displayName} · ${chat.title}``, uncut.
- Chat titles may be up to `LIMITS.title` (300, `src/core/schemas.ts`). `orchestratorTitle` (`src/main/agents/orchestratorKickoff.ts`) yields `Orchestrator · <epic title>` cut only to 300.
- `issueGrant` input (`src/core/commandSchemas.ts`, `label: z.string().min(1).max(120)`) refuses any label over 120 characters, so any epic, card or transfer chat whose agent name plus title exceeds 120 characters cannot start. Current epic titles here are ~95–110 characters, so every orchestrator chat for them fails.
- The same `grant` object goes to `issueReachCli` (project-less chats), so they share the bug.

## Change

- Name the grant label limit once (e.g. a `grantLabel: 120` entry next to the other size limits, or an exported constant beside the `issueGrant` schema) and use it in the `issueGrant` schema; do not raise or relax the limit.
- In `terminalSessions.ts`, build the chat grant label so it never exceeds that limit (cut the title part; keep the agent display name). Prefer a small named helper over inline slicing. Must not split a UTF-16 surrogate pair at the cut.
- If you add an entry to `LIMITS`, update the pinning test in `src/core/schemas.test.ts`.

## Out of scope

- Changing chat title limits, `orchestratorTitle`, the Agent access card (`GrantsCard.tsx`) form, or grant storage.

## Tests

- Regression test (TDD: write it first and see it fail) in the existing terminal sessions suite (`src/main/terminals/terminalSessions*.test.ts`, using `__mocks__/terminalSessionsRig.ts`) or a unit test for the new helper: a chat whose title makes `displayName · title` exceed 120 characters starts, and the label passed to `issueChatCli` is ≤ 120 characters and begins with the agent display name.
- An end-to-end check that a real `Workspace.issueGrant` accepts the produced label (e.g. in `src/main/agents/chatGrants.test.ts`) if the rig does not already validate it.

## Verify

Standalone fix (not in an epic): full gate — `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `npm run fireguard` (tests changed), `npm run typecheck`, `npm run deadcode`, `npm run build`.
expectedArtifacts: regression test in src/main/terminals or src/main/agents
title: Cut chat grant labels to the 120-character grant label limit
